question: Find the value of p if the shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}=(p\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k})+\mu(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$ is $\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$ units.
explanation:
**Step 1:** $a_1 = \hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}, b_1 = \hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$. $a_2 = p\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}, b_2 = 2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$.
**Step 2:** $a_2 - a_1 = (p-1)\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$.
**Step 3:** $b_1 \times b_2 = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = -3\hat{i} - 0\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$. Magnitude $|b_1 \times b_2| = \sqrt{9+9} = 3\sqrt{2}$.
**Step 4:** Shortest Distance $d = \frac{|(a_2-a_1)\cdot(b_1\times b_2)|}{|b_1\times b_2|} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$.
**Step 5:** Dot product: $-3(p-1) + 0 + 3(-2) = -3p + 3 - 6 = -3p - 3$.
**Step 6:** $\frac{|-3p-3|}{3\sqrt{2}} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \implies |-3p-3| = 9 \implies -3p-3 = 9$ or $-3p-3 = -9$.
**Step 7:** $-3p = 12 \implies p = -4$. Or $-3p = -6 \implies p = 2$.
